# Despia

The open full-stack application framework for the AI era. Describe an application once in
DespiaScript (DSX): XML-style markup + JavaScript expressions + JSON, plain text in your own
repository, and run it as a real product on every node that matters, front end to backend.
A fully dynamic kernel provides primitives; modules provide everything else; surfaces
consume. The kernel names no platform, no editor, no model and no cloud. Apache-2.0,
version 0.0.1, maintained daily by the Despia team; issues and PRs live on this repository.

The names: Despia is the framework and ecosystem. DSX is the language, the application
document format. Despia Cloud is the managed infrastructure option (builds, signing, store
delivery, hosting). Convert is the migration path for an existing web app: the easiest way
in, and one capability of the framework, not its definition.

## Five nodes, one application model

- iOS: real SwiftUI (Engine/iOS)
- Android: real Jetpack Compose (Engine/Android)
- Web: real DOM with SSR (Web, @despia/* on npm)
- Server: the backend authored in DSX in a <server> document: entities with row-level
  security, actions, API routes, workers, MCP tools; typed rejections; per-request
  budgets; table-driven deploy targets
  (Documentation/architecture/proposals/backend-authoring.md)
- CLI: a command-line program is a .dsx document
  (Documentation/architecture/proposals/cli-authoring.md)

## Start here

- README.md: what Despia is, where it comes from, how to start
- Documentation/guides/quickstart.md: a DSX app from nothing (npm create dsx)
- Documentation/guides/getting-started.md: Convert, the migration door for an existing
  web app
- Skills/writing-a-backend.md: the backend recipe: the shortest complete <server>
  document, the seam list, workers, budgets
- Documentation/reference/dsx-anatomy.md: the .dsx document anatomy (head = contract +
  state + logic, body = pure markup)
- Documentation/reference/StackReference.md: every element, attribute, value
- Skills/despiascript.md: the language pattern itself
- Skills/runtime-api.md: the full dsx surface and web contract

## The law and the proof

- Documentation/architecture/constitution.md: the architecture law
- Conformance/: the platform-neutral fixture corpus all kernels run; parity between the
  Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript kernels is falsifiable here, not asserted
- Documentation/RELEASING.md: versioning and release rules (0.0.x ladder, signed tags)

## The packages

- Engine/: the native kernel (Swift + Kotlin + shared runtime files); mirrored standalone
  to github.com/despia-native/despia-kernel
- Web/: the TypeScript kernel, compiler, DOM renderer, SSR server, CLI and scaffolder;
  ships to npm as @despia/kernel, @despia/compiler, @despia/dom, @despia/element,
  @despia/server, @despia/cli, @despia/vite-plugin and create-dsx
- AI/: on-device inference (completions, embeddings, speech, vision, tools); standalone at
  github.com/despia-native/despia-ai
- Base/: Despiabase, the on-device data plane (SQLite with vectors, snapshots); standalone
  at github.com/despia-native/despiabase
- MCP/: Model Context Protocol for apps, client and server; standalone at
  github.com/despia-native/despia-mcp
- CanvasEditor/: the visual editor SDK; the node-tree rendering of a .dsx document
- editors/: the VS Code grammar and editor integrations

## Contributing

- CONTRIBUTING.md: the workflow (issues and PRs here; patches land in the monorepo with
  authorship preserved), the fixtures-first rule, DCO sign-off
- SECURITY.md: private vulnerability reporting
- CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md: Contributor Covenant 2.1
